comparison: Perfect agreement on binding measurements (C7-C11). Both evaluations find the biophysical characterization of Orf9b peptide:Tom70 interaction using SPR and fluorescence polarization to be well-supported and compelling.

Agreement on S53E negative control (C12, C58). Both evaluations accept the mutation data showing no Tom70 binding, with OpenEval explicitly noting the structural rationale while peer reviewers implicitly accept it without raising concerns.

Strong agreement on lipid-free homodimer structure (C13-C14, C35-C36, C59-C64). Both evaluations praise the crystallographic work showing lipid stabilizes but is not required for dimerization. Peer reviewers explicitly listed this as a strength.
Complete agreement on lipid identification (C16, C39). Both evaluations accept the MS/MS data and native mass spectrometry results. Peer reviewers explicitly recognized this as a key contribution.

Agreement on apo-homodimer stability measurements (C17-C20). Both evaluations find the SEC and SPR data compelling and accept these measurements as part of the well-designed biophysical characterization.

Agreement on full-length Orf9b:Tom70 binding (C21). OpenEval notes consistency with peptide measurements, while peer reviewers accept the data as part of the kinetic model they praised. Peer R6 also covers C41-C43 which OpenEval addresses in R7 and R11.

Agreement on kinetic modeling of lipid effects (C22-C24, C42-C44). Both evaluations support the model showing lipid binding reduces homodimer dissociation rate. Peer reviewers praised the mathematical modeling approach as compelling, though OpenEval notes C24 is modeled rather than directly measured.

Disagreement on truncation mutant interpretation (C25-C27, C65-C66). OpenEval finds the data well-supported with convergent structural, biophysical, and cellular evidence. However, peer reviewers expressed uncertainty, finding it difficult to understand why the obligate monomer has similar IFN inhibition activity as WT.

Agreement on uncertainty regarding fusion construct (C29, C67-C72). Both evaluations note the disconnect between in vitro biophysical predictions and cellular functional data. OpenEval explicitly marks this as UNCERTAIN due to unresolved discrepancies, while peer reviewers found it difficult to understand the similar IFN activity.

Agreement on VOC variant analysis (C30-C34, C76-C81). Both evaluations support the findings that mutations affect homodimer stability without impacting Tom70 binding or function. Peer reviewers accepted this analysis as part of the well-designed study without criticism.

Agreement on apo-Orf9b and Tom70 complex formation (C41). OpenEval emphasizes this as a key finding resolving literature discrepancies. Peer R6 groups this with other kinetic data (C21, C42-C43) and accepts it as part of the praised kinetic model.

Partial disagreement on modeling choices (C85-C88). OpenEval finds the second-order conformational change rate constant and sensitivity analysis well-justified. Peer reviewers initially expressed uncertainty about this choice, questioning whether alternative models were explored and requesting discussion of precedence, though concerns were addressed in revision.

OpenEval evaluates background literature claims (C1-C6) as well-supported with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers typically do not assess background claims from prior literature.

OpenEval evaluates extensive background literature (C37-C54, C89-C96) as appropriately cited context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these represent established prior work rather than new findings requiring peer assessment.

OpenEval evaluates experimental design rationale for fluorescence polarization (C55-C57) as supported. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not separately assess methodological design choices that were part of the overall praised biophysical approach.

OpenEval evaluates structural rationale and negative refolding result (C67-C68) as supported. Peer R10 includes these claims as part of the fusion construct evaluation but focuses on the functional discrepancy rather than the structural measurements themselves.

OpenEval evaluates AlphaFold prediction and experimental test (C82-C84) as supported but speculative. Peer R12 includes these claims but focuses concern on the second-order rate constant modeling (C85-C88) rather than the AlphaFold-motivated experiment.

Agreement on speculative nature of biological mechanism claims (C97-C102). Both evaluations mark these as uncertain or speculative. OpenEval explicitly notes these are hypotheses rather than tested conclusions. Peer reviewers noted the biological role remains unknown as a weakness.

Peer reviewers evaluated S53E negative control for IFN suppression (C28) as supported without question. No separate OpenEval result for this specific claim, though it relates to OpenEval R2 which covers S53E binding data.
